quick.summary: How to stop writing nested queries and make your code easy to read.
quick.takeaway: Pull inner layers out. Give them clear names at the top.

beats.line: My query has five nested layers. Why does it take an hour to understand?
Think of baking a cake. Do you mix everything in one giant bowl?
You prep dry items, then wet items. One clear step at a time.
But my code is just one giant block.
Exactly. We fix it using a common table expression.
Can I just say named step?
Yes. You pull out the inner layer. Give it a name at the top.
Then my main query just calls that name. Like reading a recipe.
Exactly. It saves your team hours of decoding.

quiz.question: Why is separating a complex query into named steps helpful?
options: It runs much faster on the server.
It prevents errors with missing data.
It allows others to read the logic in clear chunks.
It automatically formats the output as a table.
quiz.explanation: Giving sections a name at the top makes the logic flow like a readable story for your team.

quiz.question: A good way to write a complex query is to nest queries inside each other.
quiz.explanation: Nesting makes queries dense and hard to untangle. Pulling them out into steps is better.
